commitResults.messageBody:
Storage methods are placeholders, so tasks and commitments cannot survive
between sessions. Implement a small versioned text codec and UTF-8 file

Write a sibling temporary file before atomic replacement to protect the
previous data on failure. Preserve next ID counters and reject corrupt
loads without returning partial state. Document the format and the
remaining console integration work in both guides and the UI plan.

commitResults.messageBody:

and its private validation helpers have limited documentation. This

Document the Save-owned types, reject null snapshots before filesystem
changes, and assert codec record counts and temporary-file placement.

output, the file format and public signatures unchanged. Update the

commitResults.messageBody:
The fork has no shared agent rules or executable ScheduleFlow UI tests.
Independent feature work needs consistent reviews and honest readiness
reporting before the five modules are connected.

Add repository-local standards skills, persistent workflow instructions,
and an isolated per-command runner with maintained JSON scenarios.
Keep planned cases distinct from successful application checks.

Keep 32 deferred feature methods explicitly unsupported, and initialize
constructor dependencies without I/O. Preserve the supplied contract.

commitResults.messageTitle: Enforce intermediate Java style in build checks
commitResults.messageBody:
The inherited Checkstyle configuration covers only the basic standard.
It misses intermediate continuation layout and undocumented public APIs,
which lets the five owners drift from the agreed project conventions.

Add whitespace and documentation checks, align switch and continuation
indentation, and fail on warnings. Document the non-bean accessors and
correct three test continuations without changing behavior or APIs.

Automating these mechanical rules keeps reviews focused on design while
retaining the skill's manual quality review and source recommendations.
The UI plan needs no expectation changes for this formatting-only work.

Validation: all 38 foundation tests and expanded Checkstyle checks pass;
packaging passes. A fresh UI session is BLOCKED by the 32 intended stubs.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle console framing across output chunks
commitResults.messageBody:
A pipe may deliver CR and LF separately, and a blank command produces
only another prompt. Treating every chunk or reply as a complete line
can report failures for correct console behavior on Windows.

Buffer an incomplete CRLF boundary and allow an explicit prompt-only
reply. Keep exact comparisons for all other bytes, capture complete
stdout at termination, and accept CRLF skill files in harness checks.
These narrow rules avoid hiding real output differences.

Validation: ten harness tests pass, including split chunks, EOF,
restart isolation, stderr, timeouts and early exits. A fresh real-code
UI preflight is BLOCKED by intended stubs; all four cases are unexecuted.

commitResults.messageBody:
A global stub gate blocks implemented commands whenever an unrelated
feature is unfinished. That can hide an active regression during the
five owners' independent implementation work.

Declare each scenario's required methods and select blocked, planned
and runnable cases separately. Stop the session on its first failure.
Keep the selection logic small enough to test independently, and record
an isolated real-JAR startup probe while Main remains a scaffold.

and a clear distinction between implemented foundations and deferred
features before branching independently.

text extraction, and replace obsolete Duke setup directions with the
ScheduleFlow commands. Add nested source and test instructions so later
sessions preserve ownership, public contracts and verification rules.

commitResults.messageTitle: Connect the console lifecycle and UTF-8 launcher
commitResults.messageBody:
The parsed commands and transactional dispatcher cannot serve users while
App, ConsoleUi and Main remain stubs. Failed startup and ordinary command
errors also need distinct recovery and process-exit behavior.

Load once before prompting, skip blank input, recover from user errors,
and exit without saving on exit or EOF. Wire UTF-8 streams and the system
clock in Main, reject extra arguments, and reuse the existing JAR entry
point. Activate five process cases and add three regression scenarios.

Verify lifecycle, saved restarts, corruption, Unicode, rollback and input
failure. Java 25 build and Checkstyle pass with 176 tests; all 12 harness
tests and UI-001 through UI-008 pass. Packaged extra arguments exit 1.
Use a writable cache and test temp folder. Rerun process checks outside
the Windows sandbox after diagnosing its native random-seed delay,
without changing application code, timeouts or expected responses.

Update both guides and the UI plan. Record the existing Save-module
format and forced-flush differences from supplied contract section 7;
preserve that owner's implementation and public interfaces. Unsupported
atomic-move and injected temp-write release checks remain unexecuted.

Null error messages can produce misleading responses, and accepting a
plan from different source data can expose a stale view of live state.
Missing stage diagnostics also make failures harder to trace.

Document API preconditions, constructors, fields and private helpers.
Reject null arguments and list elements, require a current plan source,
and describe unexpected service results with explicit exceptions.
Assert complete grammar matches and save-before-publication invariants.

Record lifecycle, parsing, dispatch, persistence and formatting stages
at FINE level. Configurable file logging provides diagnostics while
preserving normal console responses and empty stderr. Keep constructors
free of I/O and preserve existing public signatures.

Add regression coverage for rejected inputs, unchanged state and the
successful and failed save log order. Review both guides and document
the defensive contracts, assertion flags and logging setup.

Verify Java 25 build/check, all 187 JUnit tests, 12 UI-runner tests and
all eight packaged console scenarios. The packaged scenarios pass with
unchanged fixtures and timeouts outside the restricted sandbox after
its documented first-save timeout. File logging and runtime checks with
assertions disabled also pass in isolated temporary folders.

Using FINE for every diagnostic makes recoverable command failures and
fatal session errors indistinguishable when selecting a log threshold.

Use INFO for session start and normal termination, WARNING for syntax,
validation and save failures, and SEVERE for startup or input failures
that stop the session. Retain FINE for detailed stages and preserve the
original exception on each failure record.

Keep default executable console responses clean by disabling only the
console logger namespace unless an explicit logging configuration or
namespace level is supplied. Configured handlers retain normal severity
filtering, including warning-only file logging.

Update regression tests to verify severity, retained exception records,
warning-threshold filtering and both configured and default process
output. Review both guides and document severity choices and setup.

Verify Java 25 build/check and Checkstyle, all 190 JUnit tests, 12 runner

ID exhaustion, invalid saved overlaps and large duration totals. Verify

release tests. Process checks run outside the documented Windows sandbox
random-seeding delay. Unsupported atomic moves and injected temporary
write/cleanup failures remain untested.
